title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
authors: Albert Gu, Tri Dao (equal contribution, listed alphabetically)
date: December 2023 (arXiv v1 1 December 2023; v2 31 May 2024, with the same numbers in every table)
paper_note: v2; arXiv's HTML numbers several of the PDF's tables as figures, so this page uses the PDF's numbering and links the HTML anchor

code.title: state-spaces/mamba
code.note: code and checkpoints, Apache 2.0 (repo, about 20 minutes for the README and entry path); also holds Mamba-2 and Mamba-3

takeaway: Made SSM parameters (B, C, delta) input-dependent, breaking LTI so the model selectively remembers or forgets per token, and paired it with a fused parallel-scan GPU kernel; first attention-free model to match Transformer++ quality with linear-time training and 5x inference throughput, seeding today's hybrid attention-SSM production models.
verdict: Believe the mechanism: letting the input set Delta, B and C is what lets a recurrent model select, the synthetic gaps are huge, and this page's toy reproduces the selective-copying one. Read "Transformer quality" narrowly: models stop at 2.8B, every number is one run, the 5x throughput is against the unoptimised Hugging Face Transformer, and a later same-data 8B study found pure Mamba level on common zero-shot tasks but 18 points behind on 5-shot MMLU, which is why production models became hybrids.

headline.k: Selective Copying, the same Mamba block with a selective (S6) or a time-invariant (S4) layer
headline.d: the selection mechanism alone; this page's toy, same block both ways: 99.8% against 67.4%

headline.k: average zero-shot accuracy, Mamba-2.8B vs Pythia-2.8B (same data, tokenizer, 300B tokens)
headline.d: ahead on all six tasks; Pythia-6.9B scores 61.7

headline.k: generation tokens per second against a same-size Transformer (A100, prompt 2048, 128 new tokens)
headline.d: no KV cache, so far larger batches; baseline is Hugging Face transformers

resources.t: An Empirical Study of Mamba-based Language Models

resources.n: the controlled test the paper could not run: 8B Mamba, Mamba-2, Transformer and a hybrid on the same 1.1T and 3.5T tokens; where pure SSMs match Transformers and where they do not (5-shot MMLU, Phonebook, long context).
how to load the released checkpoints (for example state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf) without the CUDA kernels; the quickest way to try one.

kb.n: 2017: the architecture Mamba positions itself against; Mamba trades exact-recall KV cache for compressed recurrent state.
2022: same author (Dao) and same IO-aware philosophy; the selective scan kernel is the SSM analogue of FlashAttention's tiling and recomputation, and FlashAttention-2 is the baseline of Figure 8.
2023: attacks the KV-cache cost at serving time that Mamba removes architecturally.
2024: MoE, the other big efficiency axis; hybrids like Jamba and Nemotron 3 Nano combine both.
2022: the token budgets of Mamba's scaling-law protocol (Figure 4, Table 12).
2020: the model shapes and training recipe Mamba's scaling laws copy.
2021: rotary embeddings, part of the Transformer++ baseline and of the MHA-RoPE induction-heads baseline.
2024: the other road to a small KV cache, compressing attention (MLA) instead of replacing it.
